basic_details.job_title: CERC Research Officer Recruitment 2026 – Apply Online
basic_details.short_information: The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC), New Delhi, is engaging 03 staff consultants on the position of Research Officer (Law) in its Legal division, on purely contract basis, at a consolidated salary of Rs.75,000/- to 1,10,000/- per month depending on qualifications and experience. The essential qualification is a Graduate Degree in Law from recognized Institutes/Universities, with three to seven years of post-qualification experience. Candidates may apply online through http://vacancy.cercind.gov.in/cerc/public and send a hard copy of the Annexure-I application to the Dy. Chief

how_to_apply: Apply online through CERC's official website http://vacancy.cercind.gov.in/cerc/public.
Fill in the hard copy of the application in the prescribed proforma given in Annexure-I of the notice, with a recent passport size colour photo.
In section VI of the form, state in 100 words why you want to take up this role and are suitable for the post.
Attach self-attested copies of certificates from Tenth standard onwards, diplomas if any, and experience certificates in chronological order; use a separate signed sheet if space is insufficient.
Send the hard copy to the Dy. Chief (Admin.), 8th Floor, Tower-B, World Trade Centre, Nauroji Nagar, New Delhi 110029, so that it reaches by 11th December, 2026 up to 5.00 PM.
Applications not in the prescribed format (Annexure-I) are liable to be rejected. Incomplete applications, or those received after the due date, will be summarily rejected without any communication.
important_instructions: CERC reserves the right not to fill up all or any of the positions without assigning any reasons. CERC reserves the right to increase or decrease the number of posts at any given time. Either party may end the agreement with one month's written notice or one month's consolidated fees; a consultant leaving within one year must give three months' notice or three months' fees. Absence of more than 15 days beyond entitled leave without prior sanction, except in an emergency, may lead to termination; absence of more than 30 days without sanction and not under medical emergency makes the consultant liable to termination without notice. All official information is the property of CERC and may not be disclosed or published without written consent; the consultant shall not advise others in any matter adverse to CERC. The decision of CERC shall be final.

content_sections.heading: About CERC
content_sections.text: The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission is based at 8th Floor, Tower-B, World Trade Centre, Nauroji Nagar, New Delhi 110029. Under the Electricity Act, 2003, it regulates the tariff of central generating companies, regulates inter-State transmission, issues transmission and trading licences, adjudicates disputes and advises the Central Government on electricity policy. Its Legal Wing drafts orders and regulations, records proceedings of the Commission's hearings and defends or monitors cases in the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity, High Courts and the Supreme Court. The engagement is made under the CERC (Appointment of Consultants) (Amendment) Regulation, 2010, as amended from time to time.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Essential qualification: Graduate Degree in Law from recognized Institutes/Universities. Preferable: Master's degree in law. Experience: Three to Seven years of post-qualification experience in the legal wing in a Government Department / Private Organization / Legal firms. In addition: Applicants from Government Departments / Private Organizations should have adequate knowledge, experience and skills in research and drafting. Applicants from legal firms should have adequate knowledge of the Court procedures, besides drafting and appearance before the Supreme Court/High Courts, District Courts, quasi-judicial forums, etc. Desirable: Experience in working in Regulatory forums/Power sector. Relaxation: Relaxation in essential qualifications/experience can be considered in deserving cases. The decision of the Consultancy Evaluation Committee regarding eligibility of the candidate shall be final. Candidates should check the official notification for the complete eligibility conditions of the post.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: The Research Officer (Law) gets a consolidated salary of Rs.75,000/- to 1,10,000/- per month, depending on qualifications and experience. The professional fees are paid as a lump sum every month on completion of the month, with TDS deducted as per relevant rules. A candidate who does not submit salary slips for the past three months will be considered for selection at the minimum range of the scale. Medical benefit: Reimbursement of medical insurance for OPD/IPD treatments at ₹20,000/- per year. A consultant who has retired from Government Departments / PSUs and already avails medical facilities under any Government medical scheme is not eligible for this reimbursement. Books and periodicals: Reimbursement up to a ceiling of ₹1800/- per month. Official tour within India: By air – Economy class; by train – AC-II tier; local travel – Non-AC taxi. Escalation: In deserving cases, an annual escalation up to 10% on the fee may be given with the approval of the Chairperson, based on the previous year's performance. Duration of contract: The contract is initially for one year. On satisfactory performance, the engagement shall be extended for a further three years. After that, on continued satisfactory performance, it may be extended for up to a maximum of two years, limited to a total period of six years. The engagement is on purely contract basis and gives no right to claim regular appointment or continued contractual engagement in CERC. Working hours and leave: Normal working hours are 9.30 A.M to 6.00 P.M (05 days week), including half an hour lunch break; the consultant may be called on Saturdays, Sundays and gazetted holidays, or beyond working hours, in case of exigencies. Besides Central Government holidays, the consultant gets 15 days' leave in a calendar year, credited quarterly: 04 days each in January–March, April–June and July–September, and 03 days in October–December. Unused leave is not carried forward or encashed, and no other leave is admissible. Absence beyond these 15 days earns no professional fees; sick leave needs a medical and fitness certificate.

content_sections.heading: CERC Research Officer (Law) Job Description
content_sections.text: Scrutiny of petitions, preparation of deficiency statements for compliance by stakeholders, examination of legal issues raised in petitions and registration of petitions as per the check list. Preparation of fact sheets of cases and inputs on legal issues, coordination with various divisions, up-dation of files in RIMS/e-office and preparation of MIS reports. Attending court hearings, assisting in preparing draft Record of proceedings (ROPs) and Orders, and researching issues raised in petitions with relevant case laws. Proper maintenance of files and linking of relevant documents in files. Drafting of writ petitions/replies/rejoinders/applications/written submissions etc. for filing before the Supreme Court/High Courts/APTEL and other forums. Other works as may be assigned from time to time.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for CERC Research Officer (Law)
content_sections.text: Apply online through CERC's official website http://vacancy.cercind.gov.in/cerc/public . Fill in the hard copy of the application in the prescribed proforma given in Annexure-I of the notice, with a recent passport size colour photo. In section VI of the form, state in 100 words why you want to take up this role and are suitable for the post. Attach self-attested copies of certificates from Tenth standard onwards, diplomas if any, and experience certificates in chronological order; use a separate signed sheet if space is insufficient. Send the hard copy to the Dy. Chief (Admin.), 8th Floor, Tower-B, World Trade Centre, Nauroji Nagar, New Delhi 110029, so that it reaches by 11th December, 2026 up to 5.00 PM. Applications not in the prescribed format (Annexure-I) are liable to be rejected. Incomplete applications, or those received after the due date, will be summarily rejected without any communication.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Selection is through interaction. A written examination shall be conducted, if required, based on the decision of the Consultancy Evaluation Committee (CEC). Only candidates who strictly fulfil the eligibility criteria will be shortlisted and called for the written examination. Only candidates who qualify in the written examination will be called for interaction and presentation. Final selection is based on the ranking/merit of the combined score of qualification, experience, written examination and interaction. Candidates called for interaction must bring original documents relating to qualification, experience and salary slips for the past three months; these are examined before the interaction. No TA/DA is admissible for attending the written examination and interaction at New Delhi.
